changelog:
COURIER (v8.1.0) - Nothing is lost in transit, and every screen tells the same truth. This is a minor release rather than a patch because two behaviours change: a signal that used to be dropped when a peer was unreachable is now queued and delivered later, and a node can no longer acknowledge its own signals through any path.
- [ADD] Store-and-forward outbox. A broadcast or Direct message that reaches no one is no longer lost. The transmitter now records how a delivery failed, queues it, and the Radar Sweep - which already knows which peers are up - spends the queue on the next pass. Before this, a peer that was rebooting, a laptop with its lid closed or a DNS entry momentarily gone silently cost the operator a delivery they believed had happened; the only trace was a line in a log nobody reads. Bounded on every axis: exponential backoff capped at an hour, eight attempts, a seven-day age limit and a hard ceiling on queue depth.
- [ADD] Queued deliveries are visible. The Radar Sweep's response line reports how many are waiting, how many were just delivered and how many expired, so a queued signal is something the operator can see rather than something that only exists in the database.
- [SECURITY] Self-resonance is now refused by the server. v8.0.2 hid the ROGER THAT button on your own transmissions but left the endpoint open, so a direct POST still recorded you acknowledging yourself. Hiding a control is not a rule. The transmitter now requires the acknowledged signal to be incoming, and the receiver refuses to record a resonance against anything that is not one of its own local signals.
- [FIX] The acknowledge button no longer builds an inline JavaScript string from a remote-supplied value. The AJAX Timeline path interpolated the target URL into an onclick attribute UNESCAPED while the two template paths escaped it - so the same button was safe in two places and injectable in the third. A peer could register an alias containing a double quote and add an attribute of their choosing to the button. The target now travels in a data attribute and the handler reads it; a test parses the emitted tag back and fails if a value becomes an attribute.
- [FIX] One malformed media_url could take the whole Timeline down. A JSON payload that decoded to something other than an array reached array_slice() and raised a TypeError. Malformed attachment data is now ignored instead of fatal.
- [CHANGE] The public landing page no longer uses its own vocabulary. It said LOCAL_TRANSMISSION and FROM where the Timeline and the Vault said LOCAL_AUTHOR and INCOMING FROM - two sets of words for one concept, which is how the v8.0.2 mislabelling happened. There is now one set.
- [CHANGE] A relay of somebody else's signal can no longer be acknowledged. The button is gone from relays as well as from your own transmissions, and the server enforces it. A relay row is local, has no remote author to notify, and its counter could therefore only ever move on your own screen: an acknowledgement nobody receives is noise presented as a metric.
- [ARCH] core/render.php: the source label, the media matrix, the acknowledge button and the relay button existed in five separate places, and every one of them had to be fixed separately - v8.0.2 fixed the Vault's label while the Timeline needed its own fix, and the escaping gap above existed only in the third copy. They are now written once. This is why the release is called what it is: a fix lands once, or it lands five times and gets missed.
- [ARCH] core/outbox.php holds the whole delivery policy in one place, including the one judgement call worth stating: a delivery is queued ONLY when the target never answered at all. An ally that answered with an error is deliberately not retried, because a broadcast carries no idempotency key - api_inbox's anti-loop shield compares origin_id and a plain post leaves that empty - so a retry after a post-insert failure would publish the operator's signal a second time on a peer's timeline. Losing one delivery is bad; posting it twice on somebody else's node cannot be undone from here.
- [NOTE] tests/render_test.php and tests/outbox_test.php are new, and both run in CI. The render checks include an attribute parser that reads an emitted button back and fails if a value escaped its delimiters; pointed at the v8.0.4 markup it reports the injected attribute, so the check is known not to be vacuous rather than merely green. The outbox checks cover backoff, the attempt ceiling, expiry, queue bounds, the exclusive lock, that an unreachable peer is kept rather than lost, and that a refused target is not retried forever.
- [NOTE] The successful-delivery path needs a peer that resolves, speaks HTTPS and answers on the public internet - the outbound guard refuses anything else by design, so there is no local stub to point it at. It was verified against a sandbox node over real HTTP instead, including the case that matters most: with two allies, one silent and one answering, exactly one row is queued, for the silent one.
- [NOTE] Carries forward the v8.0 security overhaul and the v8.0.1 through v8.0.4 fixes. See RELEASE_NOTES.md.
